lesson.title: Folds that collide
lesson.subtitle: P4 nets revision
lesson.objective: Fold a six-square net that does not make a cube and find the squares that land in the same place.
lesson.story: This net of six labelled squares can be folded on screen, but it will not make a cube.

steps.title: Find the squares that meet
steps.prompt: This net does not fold into a cube. Fold every crease. Which two squares land on the same place?
hints: Fold the creases one at a time and watch where each square goes.
When every crease is folded, two squares lie on top of each other. Their edges are drawn dashed.
Squares that share a crease never land on the same place. Look at squares further apart in the net.
B and F land on the same place. Choose B and F.

steps.title: Find the open face
steps.prompt: Because two squares meet, one face of the cube has no square on it. Which face is it?
hints: Fold every crease again and turn the view to look all round the shape.
Five faces of the cube have a square. One face is open, like a box with no lid.
Find the open face, then look at the face across the cube from it. Which letter is there?
The face opposite E has no square. Choose The face opposite E.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why does this net not fold into a cube?

choices.label: Two squares land on the same face, so another face is left open.
It has the wrong number of squares, so it cannot cover every face.
Its squares are not all joined to each other edge to edge in the net.

hints: Six squares joined edge to edge is the right start for a cube.
Think about what happened when you folded every crease.
Choose the explanation about two squares landing on the same face.
